newsitem.title: TANZANIA: New Zealander jailed for two years in Zanzibar.
newsitem.headline: New Zealander jailed for two years in Zanzibar.

text.p: A Zanzibar court sentenced a New Zealand man to two years in jail and a lashing after he pleaded guilty to charges of loitering and negligence, a British diplomat said on Tuesday.

Mark Philip Cummings, 29, entered the plea and was sentenced last week by a magistrates court on Zanzibar, Carl Salisbury, the British honorary consul on the semi-autonomous island, told Reuters by telephone.
"It's actually two years and some lashes to go with it," said the diplomat, adding the number of lashes was unspecified.
The British High Commission in mainland Tanzania followed the case on behalf of New Zealand.
Salisbury said Cummings's lawyer had appealed against the sentence and the appeal would be heard on Friday after the public prosecutor failed to appear at a scheduled hearing on Tuesday.
Salisbury said the jail term was given for what was the equivalent of vagrancy.

"All the police could charge him with was being a vagrant or vagabond. They couldn't think of anything else," he said. "We thought this was going to be a slap on the wrist and a fine of 20,000 bob ($32).
"When he was sentenced to two years I couldn't believe it. We're stunned," he added.
He said Cummings was a former New Zealand army engineer and the New Zealand High Commission in Pretoria in South Africa, the nearest diplomatic mission, had notified his parents.
Cummings was arrested on August 8 for being in a restricted area which has a military camp and an electrical sub-station connecting Zanzibar to the national power grid on the mainland.
At his first court appearance on August 11, Cummings pleaded not guilty to the charges. It was not clear why he changed his plea.

Salisbury said the New Zealander arrived in Zanzibar by sailing dhow on August 3 from the northern mainland port of Tanga and set up a campsite in Fumba district, 15 km (eight miles) west of Zanzibar town.

He was arrested after local people told the military about a suspicious foreigner camping in the forest. Salisbury said Cummings opted to camp because he had a pet dog and pets were banned from Zanzibar guest houses.
He said Cummings was being held in Kilimani jail in Zanzibar town and was in good health and cheerful but "a bit upset" at the sentence.
He said he planned to visit the man later on Tuesday.
Zanzibar, a major tourist destination, joined with mainland Tanganyika to form the United Republic of Tanzania in 1964. ($1=618.75)
